map.CUID（Collision-resistant Unique Identifi: A CUID (Collision-resistant Unique Identifier) is designed to resist collisions both on a single machine and across a distributed fleet. Its structure is: a lowercase c prefix + a timestamp (base36, which keeps IDs roughly ascending in generation order) + a per-process counter (incremented within the same millisecond so one process cannot collide with itself) + a client fingerprint (a hash of browser or process characteristics that separates machines) + randomness. Compared with UUID v4 it is friendlier to database indexes — the ordered prefix reduces page splits — but because it embeds fingerprint information it should not be used where unpredictability matters for security.
